title: Field Canvas: controlled field trials for adaptive batching, cache, and quantization guardrails
creator: Evelyn Park
description: Run a coordinated set of production-safe field trials (the 'Field Canvas') to validate adaptive batching, dynamic KV caching, and model quantization profiles across representative customer traffic. The goal is to produce repeatable playbooks and automated rollout policies that deliver >=18% unit-cost reduction for mid-tail workloads while preserving >=99.8% parity on quality signals and meeting 95th percentile latency SLOs. This ticket tracks planning, experiment matrix, rollout gating, observability dashboards, and playbook documentation for PM/Eng/DS handoff.
acceptance_criteria: Experiment matrix covering at least 6 workload profiles (low-latency chat, long context summarization, high-throughput embeddings, bursty API, background batch, mixed) is executed
Clear mapping from workload profile -> recommended config bundle (batch size, cache TTL/strategy, quant profile) documented in Console playbook
Automated rollback/gating implemented: if quality delta >0.5% or latency SLO breach on 95th percentile, rollout is paused and revert path validated
Observed median unit-token cost reduction >=18% for targeted profiles in field trials (measured over 7-day rolling window), with per-route dashboards showing cost/quality tradeoffs
Runbook and a single-page Executive summary deliverable approved by Cost Ops PM and Runtime Eng lead
milestones: M1: design experiment matrix & instrumentation plan - 2025-11-20
M2: infra harness (canary pipelines + metrics surface) - 2025-12-22
M3: small-scale canaries on internal workloads - 2026-01-14
M5: full field rollouts + playbook publication - 2026-04-15
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: hidden quality regressions for long-context prompts. Mitigation: add targeted prompt-set evals and threshold gating tied to rollback automation.
Risk: telemetry noise makes cost signal unreliable. Mitigation: add traffic-tagging, synthetic baseline traces, and median-of-means aggregation across windows.
Risk: customer opt-outs due to SLA concerns. Mitigation: provide isolated dedicated variants and guaranteed fallback to baseline model with zero-loss window during experiments.
